LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 11.3.1 REGULAR COMPARATIVE AND SUPERLATIVE ADJECTIVES

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.3: Language Use 11.3.1 Regular comparative and superlative adjectives
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 11.3.1 Regular comparative and superlative adjectives, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: Which words do we use to compare things/people?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 11.3.1 Regular comparative and superlative adjectives together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem solving- is enhanced as the learner groups things in different categories correctly.

Values:
Responsibility as the learner takes up role during a language game to practise regular comparative and superlative adjectives.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (effective communication)- as the learner describes people, things and places using regular comparatives and superlatives.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Adjectives are learnt in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:
